submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole fires on the token that names a thing or a quantity: bare numerals are its strongest class (digit tokens such as ' 7', ' 3', ' 0', '083' and ' 103' are 6-9x over-represented among its top activations and are spelled-out-proof, e.g. ' 7' 1.46 vs ' seven' 0.35), and content nouns heading a referring phrase (' details', ' features', ' fields', ' value', ' stream', ' fluids') fire reliably (19/20 nouns above 0.49 in a fixed frame), while verbs (0/20 above 0.16), adjectives, pronouns other than ' this'/' it'/' which'/' that', determiners, prepositions and word-internal fragments sit at the neuron's off floor. The response is mostly a property of the token itself (token identity explains ~60% of its variance and the nominal reading of a word beats its verbal reading, ' value' 0.74 vs 0.12, ' stream' 1.60 vs 1.32), with only a weak preference for word-final over mid-word positions, so it reads the token already present rather than preparing an upcoming one.

rival_explanations: It is a numbers-only detector, and the noun firings are weaker spillover from the same quantity signal, so swapping one content noun for another should not change activation once digit tokens are excluded.

It fires on any rare or unfamiliar token whatever its word class (rare words, rare word fragments such as ' thr' and ' wh', numbers), so rare verbs and adjectives should fire as strongly as the nouns do.

It marks the token that closes a lexical item or list entry rather than what the token denotes, so light function words at clause ends and plain verbs before a full stop should fire as strongly as nouns.

Sebelum virus corona masuk ke Indonesia sebagian masyarakat kurang memperhatikan kebersihan bahkan untuk mencuci tangan. Tetapi sejak corona menjadi pandemi yang merenggut korban jiwa banyak warga yang berlomba lomba membeli hand sanitizer.
Dengan tujuan mencegah terpapar corona ketika menyentuh benda yang pada permukaanya terdapat virus, karena salah satu penyebab penularan virus corona atau Covid 19 ketika tangan menyentuh benda seperti gagang pintu kemudian tangan menyentuh hidung atau mata.
Jika sulit menemukan hand sanitizer kenapa tidak mencoba membuatnya sendiri di rumah ternyata dari berbagai sumber yang MangCara baca, proses pembuatan hand sanitizer tidak terlalu sulit. Bagaimana cara pembuatan silahkan baca artikel ini sampai selesai.
Cara Membuat Hand Sanitizer di Rumah
Photo: WHO/Elombat D
Alat dan bahan yang diperlukan
- Gelas ukur 1000 ml
- Etanol 96 persen
- Hidrogen Peroksida 3 persen
- Gliserol 98 persen
- Air
- Botol kaca
Langkah pembuatan
- Masukkan etanol sebanyak 833 ml pada gelas ukur 1000 ml
- Kemudian tambahkan Hidrogen Peroksida sebanyak 41,7 ml kedalam gelas ukur yang telah berisi etanol
- Tuangkan 14,5 ml Gliserol
- Selanjutnya tambahkan 1000 ml air dan kesemua bahan diaduk agar tercampur
- Jika sudah tercampur pindahkan formula tersebut kedalam botol kaca bersih
- Sebelum digunakan diamkan selama 72 jam telebih dahulu, setelah itu dapat dipakai
Kandungan gliserol dapat menjaga kelembaban kulit dan ketika dicampur dengan hidrogen peroksida efektif mengatasi kuman.
Tetapi apabila hand sanitizer digunakan terlalu sering atau dalam jangka lama dapat mengakibatkan gangguan pada kulit, karena tentunya efek penggunaan zat kimia.
Ada alternatif lain untuk membuat hand sanitizer dengan bahan alami atau tidak mengadung alkohol seperti yang diracik Guru SMP Muhammadiyah program khusus Kota Barat Solo, Jawa Tengah (sumber: kompas TV), berikut cara membuatnya.
Pembuatan Hand Sanitizer Tanpa Alkohol
Bahan
- Daun sirih
- Kulit buah rambutan’
Langkah pembuatan
- Rebus daun sirih dan kulit rambutan secara terpisah
- Tunggu sampai mendidih kemudian dinginkan
- Campurkan air rebusan kedua bahan tersebut pada gelas atau wadah dengan pada permukaan gelas diberikan saringan
- Tambahkan minyak zaitun kedalam racikan pembersih tangan alami tersebut agar tangan tidak kering ketika menggunakanya
Selain kedua bahan diatas Guru SMP Muhammadiyah program khusus Kota Barat Solo juga berinovasi membuat karya ilmiah membuat cairan pembersih tangan dari bahan alami lain seperti kemangi, lidah buaya dan serbuk kulit jeruk purut.

ות אצל ילדים בגיל הרך
אחת הבעיות הרגשיות השכיחות ביותר אצל ילדים בגיל הרך הינה סף תסכול נמוך, כלומר ילדים המתקשים לקבל חוקים וגבולות או מתפרצים כשמשהו לא יוצא להם בדיוק כפי שרצו.
בפועל, סף תסכול נמוך עשוי לפגוע ביכולת הלמידה של ילדים.
לדוגמא, כשילד רוכש את הקריאה והכתיבה, אם משהו לא מסתדר לו, הוא כועס ואינו מסוגל להפנים את הנלמד.
במקרים אחרים, סף תסכול נמוך יפגע גם בקשרים החברתיים עם בני גילם ועם מבוגרים.
קושי רגשי נוסף אצל ילדים הינו רמה נמוכה של אמפתיה, שכן כדי לפתח אמפתיה, צריך להבין את רגשותיהם של הזולת, קרי, להיכנס לנעליים שלהם ולקלוט מה הם מרגישים – תופעה המתרחשת לא לפני גילאי 4-5.
מעבר לכך, בעיות רגשיות אצל ילדים בגיל הרך הופכות לעתים קרובות לבעיות התנהגות בשל הקושי של אותם ילדים להפנים נורמות חברתיות, לקבל מרות וגבולות וכן עקב נטייה לתגובות לא פרופורציונליות.
הסיבה העיקרית בגינה הורים פונים לייעוץ פסיכולוגי הינה הפרעות רגשיות והתנהגותיות, הן בקרב ילדים צעירים והן בתקופת גיל ההתבגרות, כשהמשתנה החשוב ביותר על מנת לנבא הצלחה בטיפול הינו הדרכת ההורים, כלומר, שההורים ידעו בכל רגע:
- מה לעשות וכיצד להגיב
- איך לעזור לילדיהם בשליטה בהתנהגותם
- מה למנוע ואף לאסור מהם
- ממה כדאי להתעלם
- כיצד לשוחח עם ילדיהם על הבעיות השונות

"Bats Sing, Mice Giggle" tracks many years of research by hundreds of scientists that reveals how wild animals, as well as pets, have inner, secret lives of which until recently - although many animal lovers will have instinctively believed it - we have had little proof. The authors show how animal 'friends' stay in touch, and how they warn and help each other in times of danger; how some animals problem-solve as or in some instances even more effectively than humans - and how they regulate, create, and entertain themselves and others. They show how animals express grief and reverence in ways we never thought possible. From the sleep patterns of some owls, birds and horses, as well as porpoises, who go to sleep in only one half of their brains at a time; to how schools of electric fish give off complex signals of one frequency to communicate with their mates and another frequency to locate their prey, and how Polar bears tune into quantum 'radio stations' to sense prey as far away as ten miles and under the snow, "Bats Sing, Mice Giggle" provides an unparalleled insight into animals' secret lives.

Most people agree that the stereotypical “only child” is often characterized as spoiled, pampered, a “brat,” often lacking social skills, but Penny Campbell is as far away from that description as you could possibly get. When you ask the 76-year-old Boone Hospital Center retiree what makes her tick, she quickly admits, “I love life and I like people.” Those who know her best call her a people magnet.
It was, perhaps, during those early years in Hawaii that her passion for people was cultivated. “Although I didn’t know what I wanted to be when I grew up, I knew that I wanted to work with people, and that goes back to that only child thing,” she explains. She has four adult children but remembers how, as a child, she envied people who had large families with siblings, aunts and uncles. At school, she played and studied alongside a potpourri of children from all over the world including “Asians, Japanese and military kids,” but what she most remembers about that experience is everyone being readily accepted by the Hawaiian kids.
As a little girl, she often overheard people talking about how outgoing she was and how comfortable she was around people. “As a child, I was never shy and it never bothered me to meet new people,” she says. Some even described her as gregarious, precocious. Her tenure in Hawaii was a training ground for her decades-long career helping people at Boone Hospital.
“When people have been in a few times, they get to know you and begin to look for someone they recognize…a trust relationship is built,” Campbell explains. In retirement, she still finds herself asking, “How is so and so doing? I miss that.” People often arrived at her desk nervous and stressed, wanting someone familiar with whom to talk instead of seeking out staff from social services or the chaplain’s office. It was not unusual for a total stranger to walk up to her desk and say, “I was told that you’ll know who I need to talk to and who I need to see,” she said.
And her passion for sports goes way beyond simply wearing the team colors and showing up for all the home games. Campbell knows the game! “As a seven year old, I remember watching the World Champion Kansas City Chiefs and my mother knowing every single penalty foul the referee called,” her son Chris Campbell, boasts. “She can break down a 1-3-1 defense on the basketball court and can explain the reason for a referee’s flag on the football field.” He attributes his lifelong passion for sports to his mother’s knowledge of the “inner workings” of the game.

readings.explanation: This pole fires on the token that names a thing or a quantity: bare numerals are its strongest class (digit tokens such as ' 7', ' 3', ' 0', '083' and ' 103' are 6-9x over-represented among its top activations and are spelled-out-proof, e.g. ' 7' 1.46 vs ' seven' 0.35), and content nouns heading a referring phrase (' details', ' features', ' fields', ' value', ' stream', ' fluids') fire reliably (19/20 nouns above 0.49 in a fixed frame), while verbs (0/20 above 0.16), adjectives, pronouns other than ' this'/' it'/' which'/' that', determiners, prepositions and word-internal fragments sit at the neuron's off floor. The response is mostly a property of the token itself (token identity explains ~60% of its variance and the nominal reading of a word beats its verbal reading, ' value' 0.74 vs 0.12, ' stream' 1.60 vs 1.32), with only a weak preference for word-final over mid-word positions, so it reads the token already present rather than preparing an upcoming one.

It is a numbers-only detector, and the noun firings are weaker spillover from the same quantity signal, so swapping one content noun for another should not change activation once digit tokens are excluded.

It fires on any rare or unfamiliar token whatever its word class (rare words, rare word fragments such as ' thr' and ' wh', numbers), so rare verbs and adjectives should fire as strongly as the nouns do.

It marks the token that closes a lexical item or list entry rather than what the token denotes, so light function words at clause ends and plain verbs before a full stop should fire as strongly as nouns.
